name: Hue
provinceNote: Hue is a centrally governed city.
dotReason: Worth a special trip in this corridor
summary: Vietnam’s old imperial capital on the Perfume River, with a walled citadel, royal tombs and pagodas. Spend a morning in the Imperial City, visit tombs such as Minh Mang and Khai Dinh, see Thien Mu pagoda, and eat bun bo Hue and small rice cakes. Suits history lovers; plan a citadel morning and a river evening at least.
timeNeeded: A citadel morning and a river evening, plus a day upstream for the tombs.
fee: Imperial City 200,000 VND. Tombs are separate.
getThere: Phu Bai airport is 13–15 km southeast. SE trains take about 2 h 30 to 3 h 20 from Da Nang and 12 h 35 to 14 h 12 from Hanoi.
seoTitle: Hue travel guide — Imperial City, royal tombs, Perfume River, bun bo Hue
seoDescription: The Nguyễn capital on the Perfume River: the walled Imperial City, garden tombs upstream, a dusk river walk, and bún bò Huế at Dong Ba market.
intro: Hue is the Nguyễn capital on the Perfume River: the walled Imperial City on the north bank, the royal tombs in the pine hills upstream, and a kitchen that runs from bánh nậm, the court’s banana-leaf dumpling, to a bowl of bún bò Huế inside Dong Ba market. Sleep on the south bank, the modern side, and cross Phu Xuan or Truong Tien Bridge to the walls. Kỳ Đài, the flag tower built in 1807, marks the old city across the water.

Give the first morning to the Imperial City and walk in through Ngọ Môn, the king’s gate, when it opens: 06:30 from mid-March to mid-October, 07:00 the rest of the year. Give the next day to the tombs upstream. Tu Duc’s lake garden, Minh Mang’s straight axis, and Khai Dinh’s carved hillside tomb share one four-site ticket with the Imperial City. Ride out early, because May to September runs hot.

Eat between the sights: cơm hến, rice with tiny river clams, on Hen Island across Ưng Bình bridge, and bánh khoái or bún thịt nướng along Kim Long on the ride to Thien Mu’s seven-tiered tower. At dusk, walk the river path from Truong Tien Bridge to Nghinh Lương Đình, the old royal landing. Chu Văn An, Phạm Ngũ Lão, and Võ Thị Sáu are the night streets the city calls phố Tây. Go to Hoi An instead if the old town after dark is why you came.
gettingAround: Walk the south bank and cross Phu Xuan Bridge or Truong Tien Bridge to the Imperial City. Truong Tien is also the start of the river path, which belongs to walkers: the parks centre has asked the ward police to keep electric bikes off it. The tombs are upstream along the river, and you reach them by bicycle or taxi. The city’s 2026 tourism plan proposes free visitor buses and electric boats on the Perfume and Ngự Hà rivers, but neither runs to a timetable yet.

Ga Huế is on the north–south line, 103 km from Da Nang by the railway’s kilometre board. SE trains take about 2 hours 30 minutes to 3 hours 20 minutes from Da Nang, and 12 hours 35 minutes to 14 hours 12 minutes from Hanoi. Buses to Da Nang leave Bến xe phía Nam from 05:00 to 19:00, about every 15 minutes, and take about 2 hours to 2 hours 15 minutes. Phu Bai airport is 13 to 15 km southeast of the centre. The airport said in 2024 and again in 2025 that no bus serves the terminal, so arrange a taxi or a car.

stayAreas.name: South bank
stayAreas.summary: Sleep on the south bank, the modern side of the river. You walk to Truong Tien Bridge for the river path at dusk, and across Phu Xuan or Truong Tien Bridge to the Imperial City in the morning. Kỳ Đài and the citadel walls are the view across the water.

eat: Eat bún bò Huế inside Dong Ba market, cơm hến and bún hến on Hen Island, and bánh khoái or bún thịt nướng along Kim Long on the way to Thien Mu. Bánh bèo and bánh nậm are the small steamed cakes; finish them with a few drops of fish sauce. Nem lụi is grilled pork on a skewer, rolled in rice paper with herbs. After the meal, chè is the sweet soup: corn, lotus seed, taro, or the dumpling soup with roast pork.
This is not mì Quảng or cao lầu country; those belong down the coast. Chi Lăng and Bạch Đằng, on the far side of Hen Island, are the afternoon streets.
interestsBody: Hue food is bún bò Huế at Dong Ba, cơm hến on Hen Island, bánh khoái and bún thịt nướng along Kim Long, the small steamed cakes, nem lụi from a street grill, and chè after the meal.
The Imperial City is the morning: Ngọ Môn, Thái Hòa palace, and the Forbidden Purple City inside the walls on the north bank.

The royal tombs are upstream. Tu Duc’s garden, Minh Mang’s axis, and Khai Dinh’s compact tomb share the four-site ticket with the Imperial City, 530,000 VND for an adult, valid two days from the first visit. Gia Long, Dong Khanh, and Thieu Tri have their own tickets.
Thien Mu is the seven-tiered tower in Kim Long, upstream on the north bank. Tu Hieu, Dieu De, and Bao Quoc are the other pagodas. Phu Cam is the cathedral on Phước Quả hill.
The river evening is the walk from Truong Tien Bridge to Nghinh Luong Dinh, with Kỳ Đài on the north bank.
Dong Ba is the city market: produce first, then the snacks and a bowl of bún bò Huế inside.
Thanh Toan is the tiled bridge in the vegetable plots, about 8 km southeast, by bicycle.
The night streets the city calls phố Tây are Chu Văn An, Phạm Ngũ Lão, and Võ Thị Sáu.

interestCards.title: Dining and F&B
interestCards.summary: Bún bò Huế at Dong Ba, cơm hến on Hen Island, bánh khoái on Kim Long, bánh nậm from the court kitchen, and chè after the meal.

interestCards.title: Imperial City
interestCards.summary: Walk through Ngọ Môn into the Nguyễn court: Thái Hòa palace, the ancestral temples, and the Forbidden Purple City.

interestCards.title: Royal tombs
interestCards.summary: Garden tombs in the pine hills upstream: Tu Duc’s lake, Minh Mang’s axis, and Khai Dinh’s carved stairs.

interestCards.title: Pagodas
interestCards.summary: Thien Mu’s seven-tiered tower above the river in Kim Long, then Tu Hieu in the pines, Dieu De, and Bao Quoc.

interestCards.title: River walk
interestCards.summary: The Perfume River at dusk, from Truong Tien Bridge to Nghinh Luong Dinh, with Kỳ Đài across the water.

interestCards.title: Shopping
interestCards.summary: Dong Ba, the city market: produce, dry-goods stalls, and a bowl of bún bò Huế inside.

interestCards.title: Countryside
interestCards.summary: Cycle about 8 km southeast through the vegetable plots to the tiled bridge at Thanh Toan.

interestGroups.title: Dining and F&B
interestGroups.summary: Bún bò Huế at Dong Ba, cơm hến on Hen Island, bánh khoái on Kim Long, bánh nậm from the court kitchen, and chè after the meal.

cards.title: Dining and F&B
cards.summary: Bún bò Huế at Dong Ba, cơm hến on Hen Island, bánh khoái on Kim Long, bánh nậm from the court kitchen, and chè after the meal.

interestGroups.title: Imperial City
interestGroups.summary: The Nguyễn court on the north bank, and two ticketed stops outside its walls.

cards.title: Hue Citadel
cards.summary: Walk in through Ngọ Môn at opening and on through Thái Hòa palace to the Forbidden Purple City. The court is about 600 m a side, so give it the morning.

cards.title: An Dinh Palace
cards.summary: Khải Định’s private palace on the An Cựu: a ceramic-relief gate and the three-storey Khải Tường tower, a European-style castle with murals inside.

cards.title: Nam Giao Esplanade
cards.summary: Three stacked terraces in the pines south of the citadel, where Nguyễn kings offered sacrifice to heaven and earth.

blocks.heading: The walled court
paragraphs: Give the morning to the Imperial City. The gates open at 06:30 from 16 March to 15 October and at 07:00 from 16 October to 15 March. The adult ticket is 200,000 VND, and it covers the walled court only.

blocks.heading: Not on that ticket
paragraphs: An Dinh is Khải Định’s private palace on the An Cựu. Nam Giao is the three-terrace altar south of the citadel. Each has its own adult ticket, 50,000 VND.

interestGroups.title: Royal tombs
interestGroups.summary: Six garden tombs upstream. Tu Duc, Minh Mang, and Khai Dinh share the four-site ticket; Gia Long, Dong Khanh, and Thieu Tri are separate.

cards.title: Tu Duc Tomb
cards.summary: Tu Duc’s garden tomb: Lưu Khiêm lake, the Xung Khiêm pavilion, and almost 50 buildings named for the word Khiêm. Keep this one if you keep one tomb.

cards.title: Tomb of Minh Mang
cards.summary: One straight axis of about 700 m, from Đại Hồng Môn past lakes and pavilions to the burial hill, where two rivers meet to form the Perfume.

cards.title: Tomb of Khai Dinh
cards.summary: The compact tomb on the slope of Ứng Sơn: climb the dragon stairs to the carved facade and the gilded statue of the king inside.

cards.title: Tomb of Gia Long
cards.summary: The founder’s tomb, a family of tombs across 42 pine hills with no outer wall, reached by river boat or by road and ferry.

cards.title: Tomb of Dong Khanh
cards.summary: Ngưng Hy hall beside Tu Duc’s tomb, begun as a temple to Đồng Khánh’s father. A short stop when you are already at Tu Duc.

cards.title: Tomb of Thieu Tri
cards.summary: The only Nguyễn tomb that faces northwest, about 8 km out, with rice fields for a wall and the Perfume River in front.

blocks.heading: On the four-site ticket
paragraphs: Tu Duc’s garden, Minh Mang’s axis, and Khai Dinh’s compact tomb are on the four-site ticket with the Imperial City: 530,000 VND for an adult, valid two days from the first visit. Ride out by bicycle or taxi, and start early in the hot months.

blocks.heading: Separate tickets
paragraphs: Gia Long, Dong Khanh, and Thieu Tri sell their own tickets. Dong Khanh sits beside Tu Duc. Gia Long is the farthest out, by boat or by road and the Kim Ngọc ferry.

interestGroups.title: Pagodas
interestGroups.summary: Thien Mu’s tower in Kim Long, then Tu Hieu, Dieu De, and Bao Quoc, and the cathedral at Phu Cam.

cards.title: Thien Mu Pagoda
cards.summary: The seven-tiered Phước Duyên tower on Hà Khê hill above the river. Ride out along Kim Long in the late afternoon, or stop on the way to a tomb.

cards.title: Tu Hieu Pagoda
cards.summary: A working monastery in the pines of Thủy Xuân, named by Tự Đức, where Thích Nhất Hạnh was a novice.

cards.title: Dieu De Pagoda
cards.summary: One of three Nguyễn national pagodas still standing in Hue, on the Hộ Thành river near Gia Hội bridge.

cards.title: Bao Quoc Pagoda
cards.summary: An old hillside pagoda on Hàm Long hill, given its royal name in 1747. Enter through the triple gate; give it 30 to 90 minutes.

cards.title: Phu Cam Cathedral
cards.summary: The cathedral of the Archdiocese of Hue on Phước Quả hill, a nave of tall windows and arches by Ngô Viết Thụ.

blocks.heading: The pagoda stops
paragraphs: Thien Mu is the seven-tiered tower in Kim Long, on the north bank upstream of the citadel. Tu Hieu sits in the pines of Thủy Xuân, Dieu De on the river near Gia Hội bridge, and Bao Quoc on Hàm Long hill.

blocks.heading: Phu Cam is not a pagoda
paragraphs: Phu Cam is the cathedral on Phước Quả hill, not a pagoda. Sunday mass is at 05:30, 08:00, 15:00, and 18:30.

interestGroups.title: River walk
interestGroups.summary: The Perfume River at dusk, from Truong Tien Bridge to Nghinh Luong Dinh.

cards.title: Perfume River walk
cards.summary: Walk the river path from Truong Tien Bridge to Nghinh Lương Đình, the old royal landing, with Kỳ Đài, the 1807 flag tower, across the water.

body: The river evening is the walk from Truong Tien Bridge to Nghinh Luong Dinh, with Kỳ Đài on the north bank. Make it the end of a citadel or tomb day.
After the walk, the night streets the city calls phố Tây are Chu Văn An, Phạm Ngũ Lão, and Võ Thị Sáu.

interestGroups.title: Shopping
interestGroups.summary: Dong Ba, the city market: produce first, dry-goods stalls, then the snacks and a bowl of bún bò Huế.

blocks.heading: Dong Ba Market
paragraphs: Dong Ba is the city’s market, and Vietnam Tourism sends you here first: buy produce, then move on to the snacks, bánh khoái and bánh bèo. The city’s culture department puts a bowl of bún bò Huế inside the market, so eat there too. Go in the daytime.

cards.title: Dong Ba Market
cards.summary: The city market for produce, dry-goods stalls, and the snacks, with a bowl of bún bò Huế inside. Go in the daytime.

interestGroups.title: Countryside
interestGroups.summary: The tiled bridge at Thanh Toan, about 8 km southeast, past the vegetable plots.

cards.title: Thanh Toan Bridge
cards.summary: Cycle out past vegetable plots and footbridges to an 18th-century tiled-roof bridge, with a shrine to its patron, Trần Thị Đào, in the middle bay.

body: Thanh Toan is the tiled bridge in the plots of Thủy Thanh, about 8 km southeast of the centre. Go by bicycle, the way Vietnam Tourism sends you.

season.label: February to April
season.note: Come February to April, the window Vietnam Tourism picks. From May to September the plain runs 35°C to 40°C under the foehn wind, so ride to the tombs early. Rain tops 2,700 mm a year and falls mostly from September to February, with November alone about 70 percent of it. The Perfume River has an early flood in May and June and its main flood from September to December, worst in October and November, and the coast takes about 3 to 5 storms a year. October to March is cool, 20°C to 22°C on the plain, with drizzle and fog. In a flood week, check the river path, Hen Island, and the Hai Van road that morning.

faqs.q: What does one day in Hue look like?
faqs.a: Start at the Imperial City when the gate opens, on the 200,000 VND adult ticket. Eat bún bò Huế at Dong Ba market. At dusk, walk the river path from Truong Tien Bridge to Nghinh Luong Dinh. Give a second day to the tombs upstream: Minh Mang, Tu Duc, and Khai Dinh share the four-site ticket with the Imperial City, 530,000 VND for an adult, valid two days from the first visit.

faqs.q: Does the citadel ticket include the tombs?
faqs.a: No. The Imperial City is 200,000 VND for an adult and 40,000 VND for a child from 7 to 12. Under 7 is free. Minh Mang, Tu Duc, and Khai Dinh are 150,000 VND each for an adult and 30,000 VND for a child from 7 to 12. The four-site ticket is 530,000 VND for an adult and 100,000 VND for a child from 7 to 12, and it lasts up to two days from the first visit. Gia Long is 150,000 VND for an adult, and a child from 7 to 12 is free. Dong Khanh is 100,000 VND for an adult, child free. Thieu Tri, An Dinh, and Nam Giao are 50,000 VND for an adult, child free. None of those is on the four-site ticket. The same adult price applies to an international visitor and a Vietnamese visitor. Hue residents and the other groups named in the resolution pay half.

faqs.q: Is Thien Mu Pagoda on the citadel ticket?
faqs.a: No. The city’s fee resolution prices the Imperial City and the tombs and does not list Thien Mu. Ride upstream along the north bank through Kim Long, and ask at the gate about any fee and the hours.

faqs.q: How do I get from Da Nang to Hue?
faqs.a: By train, SE services take about 2 hours 30 minutes to 3 hours 20 minutes between the two stations. Buses from Hue’s Bến xe phía Nam run 05:00 to 19:00, about every 15 minutes, and take about 2 hours to 2 hours 15 minutes. The heritage train over Hai Van Pass takes about 3 hours and stops at Lang Co. By road, the Hai Van Pass segment alone is about 22 km and nearly an hour; the tunnel is more than 12 km and 10 to 15 minutes.

faqs.q: How far is Phu Bai airport, and is there a bus?
faqs.a: Phu Bai is southeast of the centre: 13 km on the civil-aviation chart and about 15 km on the national tourism page. In replies of 29 September 2024 and 15 January 2025, the airport said no bus was serving the terminal, so arrange a taxi or a car.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Hue?
faqs.a: February to April. May to September is hot, 35°C to 40°C on the plain. The heavy rain runs from September to February, and the Perfume River’s main flood is September to December, worst in October and November. In a flood week, Hen Island can go under and the river path may be unusable, so check that morning.

In 2026 the festival runs all year in four seasons. It opened at Ngọ Môn square on 1 January 2026, the arts week is 13 to 18 June 2026, and a countdown closes it on 31 December 2026. Dates for later years are not yet published.

faqs.q: What should I eat in Hue?
faqs.a: Bún bò Huế, the beef-and-pork noodle bowl, at Dong Ba market. Cơm hến, rice with tiny river clams, on Hen Island. Bánh khoái, the turmeric crepe, and bún thịt nướng along Kim Long. Bánh bèo and bánh nậm, the small steamed cakes, and nem lụi, grilled pork skewers. Chè, the sweet soup, after the meal.
